segments.text: My mother began studying English at 60
Having been a homemaker for many years
She made the decision when her grandchild was born
At first she struggled even with pronunciation
Trying to make sounds her mouth was not used to
She would stretch her lips again and again
She patiently corrected herself from reading Tapis Tapu
But my mother was determined
She would get up at six every morning
And listen to English lessons on the radio
After breakfast, she would read the textbook for an hour
Committing words to memory
After half a year, she could handle simple daily conversation
After a year, she gave directions to a tourist
After three years, she wrote an English essay at a university extension course
My mother's progress was somewhat slow but steady
The secret was keep doing it every day
Even a short amount of time continued for three his sixty-five days
It comes a vast sum of hours
When her grandchild turned five
She began speaking English with him
The grandchild was amused to see
Is grandmother speak English?
Then he too began learning English
My mother's story teaches me something important
Too late is only an excuse
If the desire to learn is real
One can begin at any age
Modern society imposes the pressure on young people
That you must work hard while young
But in an age where people live to a hundred
Learning is a lifelong pursuit
My mother is 65 this year
She is now planning her first solo trip abroad
The destination is London
To make her own way through the world in English
That is her new dream
